stem: A hedge fund begins the year with USD 150 million and ends with USD 180 million before fees. It charges a 1.5% management fee on year-end AUM and a 15% incentive fee calculated net of the management fee, subject to a 6% hard hurdle. Total fees for the year (USD millions) are closest to:
explanation: Management fee = 0.015 × 180 = 2.70. Value after management fee = 177.30. Hurdle level = 150 × 1.06 = 159. Incentive = 0.15 × (177.30 − 159) = 2.745. Total fees = 2.70 + 2.745 = 5.45 million.

rationale.A: Incorrect. 6.80 treats the hurdle as soft, charging the incentive on the whole 27.30 gain after the management fee.
rationale.B: Incorrect. 5.85 computes the incentive on the gross value of 180 above the hurdle, ignoring that it is net of the management fee.
rationale.C: Correct. With a hard hurdle the incentive applies only to the 18.30 above the 159 hurdle level, giving total fees of 5.45.

verify: const m=0.015*180, pre=180-m, inc=0.15*(pre-150*1.06); return m+inc;

stem: A fund's high-water mark is USD 120 million. It starts the year at USD 105 million and earns a 20% gross return. The management fee is 2% of year-end AUM and the incentive fee is 20%, calculated net of the management fee, with no hurdle. The incentive fee (USD millions) is closest to:
explanation: Gross value = 105 × 1.20 = 126. Management fee = 0.02 × 126 = 2.52, leaving 123.48. Incentive applies only above the HWM: 0.20 × (123.48 − 120) = 0.70 million.

rationale.A: Correct. Only the 3.48 above the 120 high-water mark earns an incentive fee: 0.20 × 3.48 = 0.70.
rationale.B: Incorrect. 3.70 ignores the high-water mark and charges 20% on the full 18.48 gain from 105.
rationale.C: Incorrect. 1.20 uses the gross value of 126 above the HWM, forgetting to deduct the management fee first.

stem: An investor finances a real asset with USD 40 of her own cash and USD 60 of borrowed money at 4%. The asset returns 6%. The return on the investor's own cash is closest to:

rationale.A: Incorrect. 7.20% divides borrowed funds by total assets (60/100) rather than by the investor's own cash.
rationale.B: Correct. The leverage ratio is 60/40 = 1.5, so the levered return is 6% + 1.5 × 2% = 9.00%.
rationale.C: Incorrect. 7.33% inverts the ratio, using 40/60 instead of 60/40.

stem: A private equity fund pays carried interest to the GP on each profitable exit as it occurs. Which provision best protects LPs if later deals in the fund lose money?
explanation: This is a deal-by-deal (American) waterfall. If later losses mean the GP received more carry than it earned over the life of the fund, a clawback requires the GP to return the excess to LPs.

rationale.A: Incorrect. A high-water mark is mainly a hedge fund mechanism based on NAV peaks; it does not recover carry already paid on earlier exits.
rationale.B: Correct. A clawback forces the GP to repay carried interest that later losses show was not earned.
rationale.C: Incorrect. A soft hurdle actually makes the incentive fee more generous to the GP once the hurdle is cleared.
